title: TURN DOWN ONE DOOR, NOT THE WHOLE HOUSE
goal: A boundary can close one door without burning down the whole house.
steps: 1. Name Contact — Name the contact pattern you want to change without judging the person. Down Door — press feet.
2. Pick Door — Choose exactly one access door: TIME, TOPIC, CHANNEL, LOCATION, or FREQUENCY.
3. Lower One — Lower that door by one clear level: shorter call, one topic excluded, text only, public place, or fewer contacts. Down Door — split duty.
4. Hold Setting — State the new setting and leave every other door unchanged for this round. Down Door — next action.

title: UNDERSTAND, THEN DISAGREE CLEANLY
goal: Empathy does not sign their conclusion.
steps: 1. View They — Summarise their view until they could recognise it. Understand Disagree — breathe naturally.
2. Name Need — Name the need or logic you understand.
3. Say Meaning — Then say exactly where your meaning, value, or decision differs. Understand Disagree — notice detail.
4. Receive Own — No ‘but’ inside the summary; disagreement receives its own sentence. Understand Disagree — next action.

goal: Repair is a behaviour pattern, not a tone of voice.

3. Evaluate — Check the apology against those criteria rather than immediate emotion. Apology Needs — next action.

title: ONE FIGHT, THREE TIME SCALES
goal: Today’s argument should not impersonate the whole relationship.
steps: 1. Issue Recurring — Check the immediate issue, the recurring pattern, and the full relationship history separately. Fight Three — loosen hands.
2. Give Own — Give each its own conclusion and action. Fight Three — name event.
3. Don't Erase — Do not let a good history erase a harmful pattern or one incident erase all context. Fight Three — next action.

title: MAP THE RELATIONSHIP LABOUR
goal: Imbalance becomes negotiable after it becomes visible.
steps: 1. Plan Carries — Across a defined period, tally who initiates, accommodates, repairs, plans, and carries emotional follow-up. Map Relationship — soften shoulders.
2. Add Context — Include background for genuine capacity differences. Map Relationship — split forecast.
3. Use Categories — Discuss the pattern using categories, not accusations, and request one clear rebalance. Map Relationship — next action.

steps: 1. Picture Assumption — Picture the assumption driving your reaction. Ask Question — hear sound.

3. Ask Suitable — Ask at a suitable time, listen fully, and compare reply plus later behaviour with the original model. Ask Question — next action.

display.ritualText:
POSTURE WITHOUT PROPHECY

30–60 seconds · Guided reset

GOAL
The body can stop rehearsing defeat before facts arrive.

1. Adopt — Adopt a stable, non-defensive position: feet supported, spine available, gaze level, arms unguarded enough for safety. clearly refuse both positive and negative…. Posture Without — feel support.
2. Hold Posture — Hold the posture while waiting for actual evidence. Continue with Hold Posture. Posture Without — name sensation. Posture Without — next action.

WIN
✓ The body can stop rehearsing defeat before facts arrive.

FORMULA FLOW
Adopt → Hold Posture

PAUSE
Choose protective posture and distance in genuinely threatening settings.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
goal: A safer choice may be the mistake you can see early enough to correct.
steps: 1. Name Options — Name the two or three live options. For each, Picture the specific way it could fail—not a vague fear. Choose Easiest — breathe naturally.
2. Name Failure — Name the earliest observable sign that failure has begun. It must be visible or clear, not a feeling alone.
3. Warning — State what corrective action would still be available when that sign appears and what cost has already accumulated. Choose Easiest — name feeling.
4. Choose Visible — Choose the option whose reliable warning arrives while correction is still practical. Use this as one decision criterion, not the whole verdict. Choose Easiest — next action.

title: FIND THE MOMENT THE FLOOR CATCHES YOU
goal: Panic can obscure support that never disappeared.
steps: 1. Shift Weight — Stand safely and shift weight slowly left, centre, right, then forward and back. Find Moment — move slowly.
2. Identify Instant — At each transition, spot the exact instant the receiving foot supports you. Find Moment — name sensation.
3. Finish Centre — Finish at centre and name the strongest contact point. Find Moment — next action.

title: BORROW STILLNESS FROM THE WALL
goal: Let an unmoving object prove that movement is not the whole field.
steps: 1. Rest Gaze — Rest your gaze on a stable line, corner, or heavy object. Borrow Stillness — breathe naturally.
2. Compare Visual — Compare its visual constancy with the motion inside your body and mind.
3. Don't Match — Do not make the inner movement match. Borrow Stillness — name sensation.
4. Let Facts — Let both facts coexist until the outer reference becomes usable. Borrow Stillness — next action.

title: SORT THE SOUNDS BY DISTANCE
goal: Urgency shrinks when hearing regains depth.
steps: 1. Identify Nearest — Spot the nearest sound, one mid-distance sound, and the farthest audible layer. Sort Sounds — move slowly.
2. Move Attention — Move attention outward through those distances, then back once. Sort Sounds — pick action.
3. Let Far — Let the far sound widen the perceived space around the closest one. Sort Sounds — next action.

3. Don't Move — Do not move toward pleasant colours or away from unpleasant ones. Find Five — name sensation.
4. Finish Colour — Finish with the colour farthest from the trigger. Find Five — next action.

title: THE ROOM HAS JOBS, NOT DEMANDS
goal: A room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations.
steps: 1. Scan Objects — Choose four safe visible objects without moving toward them. Avoid screens if they add strain. Room Has — breathe naturally.
2. Name Jobs — For each object, name only its ordinary job: chair supports, lamp lights, cup holds, door opens.
3. Drop Demands — Say ‘not needed now’ to every function that does not serve the current safe moment. Do not remove or organise anything. Room Has — pick action.
4. Choose Helper — Choose the one object whose real function supports the next action, then use only that function. Room Has — next action.

title: COUNT EVERY OPEN LOOP
goal: Invisible commitments keep using memory until named.
steps: 1. Question Task — Name every unresolved promise, question, task, decision, and waiting item without solving any. Count Every — loosen hands.
2. Use Line — Use one line each. Count Every — notice detail.
3. Imagine Boundary — When nothing else appears for thirty seconds, Imagine a boundary around the inventory and choose a separate processing time. Count Every — next action.

title: ONE ACTIVE SLOT
goal: Short-term attention needs a deliberate admission policy.
steps: 1. Create Positions — Create three positions: ACTIVE, WAITING, ARCHIVE. Active Slot — widen gaze.
2. Wait Route — Put only one concern in active, one likely next item in waiting, and route everything else to archive with a retrieval Notice. Active Slot — notice detail.
3. Give Active — Give the active concern a protected time box. Active Slot — next action.

title: HIDE THE OPTION NAMES
goal: See what the options look like before their names start campaigning.
steps: 1. Mask Names — Ask someone—or a shuffled Notice—to rename the leading options A, B and C without showing which is which. Hide Option — soften shoulders.
2. Choose Traits — Choose three relevant traits, such as cost, time, fit, reliability, or learning. Keep safety facts visible.
3. Rank Blind — Compare the symbols on those traits without guessing their identities and Hold the current order. Hide Option — split forecast.
4. Reveal Options — Reveal the names. Keep the blind order or name exactly what Name changed it and why. Hide Option — next action.

1. Mask Names — Ask someone—or a shuffled Notice—to rename the leading options A, B and C without showing which is which. Hide Option — soften shoulders.
2. Choose Traits — Choose three relevant traits, such as cost, time, fit, reliability, or learning. Keep safety facts visible.
3. Rank Blind — Compare the symbols on those traits without guessing their identities and Hold the current order. Hide Option — split forecast.
4. Reveal Options — Reveal the names. Keep the blind order or name exactly what Name changed it and why. Hide Option — next action.

WIN
✓ See what the options look like before their names start campaigning.

FORMULA FLOW
Mask Names → Choose Traits → Rank Blind → Reveal Options

PAUSE
Never hide facts required for safety, consent, ethics, affordability, or professional decision support.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

Identify Decision → State Action

PAUSE

title: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
goal: Motivation can guess; one work pulse can measure.
steps: 1. Run Pulse — Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it. Find Working — move slowly.

3. Read Strain — Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting. Find Working — pick action.
4. Set Gear — Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio. Find Working — next action.

4. Increase — Increase future doses slowly. Boring Dose — next action.

3. Select Path — Delay preference until evidence selects the path. Plan Both — next action.

title: FIVE CLUES MAY BE ONE CLUE
goal: Several clues can be one echo wearing different clothes.
steps: 1. Name Clues — Name up to five clues currently supporting the worried conclusion. Five Clues — soften shoulders.
2. Link Sources — Imagine a line between clues that came from the same person, event, article, assumption, mood, or repeated retelling.
3. Collapse Copies — Collapse every linked cluster into one source family; do not count its echoes separately. Five Clues — notice detail.
4. Recheck Claim — Recheck the claim using the number and quality of independent families that remain. Five Clues — next action.

title: THE LAST-DAY FILTER
goal: Finite life can expose counterfeit urgency.
steps: 1. Imagine Back — Imagine looking back from life’s end—not to frighten yourself, but to rank. Last Day — loosen hands.
2. Demand — Which current demand disappears?
3. Remain Relationship — Which relationship, integrity choice, health need, or contribution remains?. Last Day — pick action.
4. Give Surviving — Give the surviving priority one concrete slot today. Last Day — next action.

goal: Extended thinking is earned by a clear question and output.

2. Return Direct — If either is missing, deny the session and return to direct life. Return Direct next. Thoughts Must — allow opposite. Thoughts Must — next action.

title: CHANGE THE MENTAL TOOL, NOT THE PRESSURE
goal: Wrong mental mode makes effort repeat itself.
steps: 1. Decide Accept — Classify the demand as SOLVE, DECIDE, FEEL, ACCEPT, COMMUNICATE, or WAIT. Change Mental — widen gaze.
2. Name Mode — Name the mode currently running. Change Mental — pick action.
3. Choose Shut — Shut it down and perform the first action belonging to the correct mode—calculate, choose, allow, release, speak, or schedule. Change Mental — next action.

title: REPLAY THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
goal: Find the turning point, not another theory about the whole conversation.
steps: 1. Recall Exchange — Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different. Replay Turning — breathe naturally.
2. Halve Speed — Replay it once in imagination at half speed. Keep to observable words, pauses, volume, face, and movement.
3. Shift — Stop at the first change and name it without motive: ‘the pause lengthened,’ ‘the volume rose,’ or ‘the reply shortened.’. Replay Turning — pick action.
4. Keep Fact — Keep that one fact. End the replay before building another explanation. Replay Turning — next action.

title: GIVE THOUGHTS WEIGHTED VOTES
goal: Mental statements should not all receive one ballot.
steps: 1. Score Evidence — For each influential thought, score evidence, relevant expertise, recency, and decision relevance. Give Thoughts — move slowly.
2. Multiply — Multiply nothing; simply rank. Give Thoughts — pick action.
3. Let Highest — Let the highest-quality thought advise the action while lower-ranked voices remain recorded but nonbinding. Give Thoughts — next action.

2. Total — Total the four ratings.
3. Protect Block — Award one protected block to the highest bidder and deny all others entry until time expires. Auction Next — pick action.
4. Update Evidence — Re-auction with updated evidence. Auction Next — next action.

title: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
goal: A loop is easier to spot when it has to fit on five tiles.
steps: 1. No Sentences — Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences. Turn Loop — widen gaze.
2. Imagine Five Signs — Give each of the last five thought turns one simple mental picture.
3. Spot The Return — Notice the first picture whose meaning comes back later. Turn Loop — notice detail.
4. Choose An Exit — At the next box, picture one real fact to check or one small action to take, then stop imagining. Turn Loop — next action.

title: WHERE EXACTLY IS THE OBSERVER?

steps: 1. Search Carefully — Search carefully for the boundary, size, and location of the one who observes. Where Exactly — hear sound.

3. Observe Found — Every found sensation is itself observed. Where Exactly — split duty.
4. Rest Inability — Rest with the inability to locate a final point. Where Exactly — next action.

title: SOFTEN BOTH SIDES OF SEEING
goal: Perceiver and perceived need not stay rigidly opposed.
steps: 1. Choose Simple — Choose a simple object or sound. Soften Both — press feet.
2. Attend Time — Attend at the shared time to its qualities and the act of perceiving.
3. Place Reality — Refuse to place all reality on either side. Soften Both — notice detail.
4. Let Relationship — Let the relationship event—seeing or hearing—become primary for several seconds. Soften Both — next action.

title: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT

4. Finish Unit — Finish one complete task unit using feedback—not self-opinion—to make corrections. Put Commentator — next action.

3. Choose Position — Choose the position best suited to the upcoming task rather than declaring any one neutral. Rotate Observation — next action.

title: THE MILLISECOND BEFORE THE NAME
goal: What you notice exists briefly before concept files it.
steps: 1. Look Touch — Look at or touch something ordinary. Millisecond Before — loosen hands.
2. Catch Bare — Catch the first bare instant before ‘cup,’ ‘cold,’ ownership, or preference appears.
3. Don't Freeze — Do not freeze it; simply recognise the order: contact, then concept. Millisecond Before — notice detail.
4. Repeat Sound — Repeat with a sound. Millisecond Before — next action.

title: PLAY EMOTION JENGA
goal: Pull one feeling from the stack and see what is actually holding.
steps: 1. Name Stack — Name two or three feelings and place each on a separate mental or your imagination block. Play Emotion — soften shoulders.
2. Pull One — Temporarily bracket one block with the phrase ‘not deleted—just outside this test.’
3. Check Remainder — Observe what changes in the remainder: body location, urge, story, intensity, or nothing at all. Keep one difference. Play Emotion — name feeling.
4. Rebuild Stack — Restore the removed block. Repeat only if useful, then rebuild the complete stack before finishing. Play Emotion — next action.

title: SCULPT THE PROBLEM
goal: Abstract distress changes when relationships become physical.
steps: 1. Use Small — Represent the problem using small objects for people, obstacles, resources, and goals. Sculpt Problem — feel support.
2. Feel Arrange — Arrange them as they feel now.
3. Move Object — Move only one object or distance to create a more workable configuration. Sculpt Problem — pick action.
4. Name Real — Name the real-life action equivalent to that move. Sculpt Problem — next action.

title: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
goal: Resistance may be protecting something your plan ignored.
steps: 1. Give Obstacle — Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting?. Interview Obstacle — move slowly.
2. Ask Fear — What do you fear will happen?
3. Make Step — What would make one step acceptable?. Interview Obstacle — pick action.
4. Picture Negotiate — Picture its answers, then negotiate a small action that protects the valid need without handing over total control. Interview Obstacle — next action.

title: WHICH REGRET ARE YOU AVOIDING?

steps: 1. Estimate Regret — For each option, estimate regret of action, inaction, delay, and self-betrayal. Which Regret — move slowly.
2. Describe Future — Say the future scene behind the highest score. Which Regret — split duty.
3. Ask Regret — Ask which regret is reversible and which conflicts most with your values. Which Regret — next action.

title: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
goal: Crowded choices get clearer when only two enter each round.
steps: 1. Seed Options — Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival. Two Option — soften shoulders.
2. Pick Criterion — Choose one criterion that matters for this round and Picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Play Pairs — Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion. Two Option — notice detail.
4. Crown Next — Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict. Two Option — next action.

title: REMOVE WHAT THE CHOICE WOULD ‘PROVE’
goal: Identity signalling can distort an otherwise practical decision.
steps: 1. Say About — Name what each option would supposedly say about you—successful, loyal, brave, weak, ordinary. Remove Choice — hear sound.
2. Cross Out — Strike through those identity messages mentally.
3. Check Again — Re-check only consequences, values, constraints, and evidence. Remove Choice — split duty.
4. Notice Shift — Notice whether the preferred option changes. Remove Choice — next action.

PAUSE
Identity and community may be legitimate values; distinguish them from performance.

title: WHOSE HANDWRITING IS ON THIS BELIEF?
goal: Inherited rules often feel like your own after the source fades.
steps: 1. Name Modelled — Name who modelled, rewarded, enforced, or normalised the belief. Whose Handwriting — loosen hands.

title: MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS
goal: A rule must survive context before it earns the word universal.
steps: 1. State Rule — Picture the rule without naming who taught it. Move Rule — widen gaze.
2. Change Context — Place it in three contrasting settings—for example family, workplace, and friendship—with different power and consequences.
3. Compare Effects — Compare who is protected, restricted, or harmed in each setting. Move Rule — challenge answer.
4. Keep Core — Keep only the part that remains ethical and workable across contexts; Notice the rest as conditional. Move Rule — next action.

title: RETURN THE SHAME TO ITS OLD ADDRESS
goal: A judging context can end while its standard keeps living inside you.
steps: 1. Identify Whose — Spot whose rule the shame is enforcing and the setting where it was learned. Return Shame — loosen hands.
2. Ask Whether — Check whether you still endorse that standard. Return Shame — split duty.
3. Keep Repair — Keep any ethical repair that is truly yours; return contempt, prejudice, or impossible expectation to its source. Return Shame — next action.

title: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
goal: A rule may fit one situation without ruling your whole life.
steps: 1. Name The Belief — Say the belief silently. Give Belief — widen gaze.
2. Imagine Four Limits — Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Test Inside — Picture one real case where it fits. Give Belief — split duty.
4. Test Outside — Picture one real case where it does not fit.
5. Set Its True Place — Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief. Give Belief — next action.
